title: The iqamah
hook: the second call, just before prayer begins

segments.voice: Yesterday, the adhan's words, and your line: come to success. What did you notice the call names as success? The adhan says the time has come. Today, the call that says now. Day one thousand seventy-nine.

Inside a mosque, a few minutes after the adhan. The room is loose and quiet. A teenager scrolls his phone by the wall. Two old friends murmur near the back. Someone prays a couple of units alone in a corner. A boy is tying and retying his shoelace for no reason. Then a man near the front stands and starts a second call, quicker than the first, flatter, almost brisk. And the whole room changes shape. Phones go into pockets. People rise, step forward, line up shoulder to shoulder, and close the gaps between them. By the time he finishes, there are rows where there was a crowd.
screen: `A LOOSE, QUIET ROOM.` → `A SECOND CALL, QUICKER.` → `ROWS WHERE THERE WAS A CROWD.`

segments.voice: That second call is the iqamah. The adhan goes out to the street: the time has come, wherever you are, come. The iqamah is for the room: the prayer is starting, here, now. Its words mostly follow the adhan, and Sahih al-Bukhari, number 605, records how Bilal was told to say them: the adhan's phrases in pairs, the iqamah's singly, except for one new line that the adhan doesn't have. Qad qamati as-salah. The prayer has stood up. It has begun. The Hanafi school says the iqamah's phrases in pairs, like the adhan, and the other Sunni schools say most of them singly; each follows reports it trusts. Between the two calls there's a space. In Sahih al-Bukhari, number 624, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says that between every two calls there is a prayer, for whoever wants it. It's a waiting room with a door already open. And then there's how to arrive when you hear the iqamah. A sprint might seem right. The hadith says the opposite. Sahih al-Bukhari, number 636: when you hear the iqamah, walk to the prayer with calm and dignity, don't hurry; whatever you catch, pray it, and whatever you missed, complete it afterward. So the call that says now doesn't mean panic. It means stand, step in, and join the row as you are. The adhan gathers people from far away. The iqamah gathers the people already in the room into one line.
screen: `THE ADHAN FOR THE STREET, THE IQAMAH FOR THE ROOM.` · `QAD QAMATI AS-SALAH: IT HAS BEGUN.` · `BETWEEN THE TWO CALLS, A PRAYER.` · `WALK, DON'T RUN.` · then, large: `THE PRAYER HAS STOOD UP.`

segments.voice: The practice: stand at the iqamah. If you're sitting, notice it first: the looseness, the scrolling, the half-attention of waiting. Now, without rushing, stand up. Feel your feet take your weight. Let your shoulders settle and your hands rest. That's the moment the room changes shape. Stay standing, or sit again if you need to, and breathe slowly in the space after the call. If you pray, you can stand this way at your next prayer, calm, not hurried. If you don't, this is simply the difference between waiting and beginning. The bell holds the time.
Iqamah. The second call, said in the room just before the prayer begins, with its own line: the prayer has stood up. Today's word.

Your line: stand now. Today, when something you've been waiting for finally starts, step into it calmly, without a sprint and without a delay. Tomorrow, the sunnah prayers. Day one thousand seventy-nine.

howItsDone: In the mosque, someone calls the iqamah just before the congregational prayer starts; the worshipers stand, form straight rows behind the imam, and the prayer begins. It may also be said by someone about to pray alone.

original.note: Arabic: the second call, said as the prayer begins.

trapdoor: what you thought: the iqamah is just the adhan said again.
what it means: a second, quicker call for the room, with its own line: the prayer has stood up.
what a scholar hears: Bilal's pairs and singles in Bukhari 605, the prayer between the two calls in 624, and the calm walk of 636.

notes: Hadith numbers to confirm: Bukhari 605 (Anas: Bilal ordered to say the adhan in pairs and the iqamah singly, except qad qamati as-salah, per a related narration); Bukhari 624 ('Abdullah ibn Mughaffal: between every two calls is a prayer, for whoever wishes); Bukhari 636 (Abu Hurayrah: come with calm and dignity when you hear the iqamah).

School difference: Hanafi doubled iqamah vs single in the other Sunni schools; Ja'fari practice also has its own form (pairs, with the Shia additions). Confirm the wording and whether to name the Ja'fari form.
howItsDone says the iqamah may also be said before praying alone; confirm.

Editor: school difference narrowed to 'the other Sunni schools ... most of them singly' (Shafi'i and Hanbali double qad qamati; Ja'fari uses pairs); removed telling the listener what they'd expect; carry names tomorrow.
